bug_info.bug_desc: In full arbitration mode (DstWrReq), the StIdle state starts a hardware transaction whenever dst_update_i is asserted, without checking whether the incoming destination sample dst_ds_i actually differs from the last handshake-completed value in dst_qs_o. This violates the spec requirement that a hardware update indication which does not result in a value change must not start a transaction. As a result, a same-value or continuously asserted dst_update_i can repeatedly re-enter StWait and generate spurious hardware-update handshake events, leading to assertion failures.
bug_info.fix_hint: Qualify the incoming destination update indication with a value-change check before using it to start a transaction. Create a local signal such as dst_update = dst_update_i & (dst_qs_o != dst_ds_i) and use dst_update in the StIdle state transition instead of the raw dst_update_i. This suppresses handshake generation when the observed destination value is unchanged from the value already completed in the handshake, while still allowing genuine hardware changes to be reported.
